extension.summary: Rivulet: watch Stremio-protocol catalogs, addons and streams in Kodi
extension.description: Rivulet is a Kodi client for the Stremio addon protocol: browse and search catalogs by type, install community Stremio addons from a manifest URL, resolve streams and play them back through an embedded or remote stremio-server-go streaming server, and optionally sync your addon collection with your Stremio account.
extension.disclaimer: This addon does not host, index or provide any media content. It is a client for third-party Stremio addons that you install yourself.
extension.news: v0.19.0: - New: an add-on can now be switched off instead of removed. Until now the add-on manager offered only install and remove, so silencing a source that returned nothing useful - or an official add-on that cannot be removed at all - meant losing its settings and reinstalling it from its manifest URL later. Picking an add-on now opens a short menu with Disable (or Enable) and Remove. A disabled add-on stays installed and keeps its place, but is no longer asked for catalogs, titles, streams or subtitles, and its catalogs stop lighting up Home's rows. The state is local to this Kodi box and is not pushed to your Stremio account. v0.18.0: - New: "Continue watching" and "Library" are now one "Continue" screen. They were largely the same list - a title you are part-way through is usually also one you saved - so two Home rows meant guessing which one held what you wanted. The new screen shows everything at once in four labelled rows: what you are part-way through, what to play next, what you have finished, and what you saved but never started. A title that was in both lists now appears once. The played rows are read from Rivulet's own records, so they work when you are logged out or offline, where "Library" could only offer "Login to Stremio". - Fix: a series vanished from "Continue watching" the moment you finished an episode - exactly when you wanted the next one. Watching an episode to the end took the whole show off the row, so on one setup two shows being actively watched were hidden while three barely-started films stayed. Finished shows now move to a "Next up" row that names the episode to play next, such as "S1E3", and only move to "Recently watched" once there is genuinely nothing left. - Fix: three faults on the new screen that only showed on a television. A row could come up blank and leave the screen unresponsive until you pressed Back; a title's progress bar ran wider than its poster; and the highlight around the focused poster fell 32 pixels short of the artwork on every row. v0.17.0: - Improved: searching now returns one row per title, with the closest matches first. Every add-on that can search was asked the same question and the answers were simply stacked, so a title came back once per add-on that had it - on one setup "alien" filled the browser with 96 posters covering 57 actual titles, and 41% of what you scrolled through was something already passed. Duplicates are now collapsed into a single row that keeps the fullest information of the copies, since each add-on trims its search results differently. Order follows what you typed: an exact title first, then titles starting with it, then titles containing it as a word. Within those, the better-known title leads - "alien" now opens on the 1979 original, where before "My Stepmother Is an Alien" could sit above "Aliens". Titles that merely share a name still each get their own row. - Improved: in the poster browser, the focused title's year, rating and runtime are now one flowing line instead of three fixed-width boxes. Kodi cannot size a box to its text, so the one width had to fit everything and fitted nothing: a series' year range was cut short ("2010-2017" showed as "2010..." on Sherlock) while a runtime pressed against both edges. The rating also now says "IMDb 9.0" rather than a bare coloured number, which was as easy to read as a percentage or a season count. - Fix: a series still running showed a dangling dash after its start year - "2022–" - on the poster browser, the title screen and the source list. It now reads "2022–now", translated in every supported language. v0.16.1: - Fix: 0.16.0's new logo reached everything except the place you look at most - the mark drawn in the header of Rivulet's own screens still showed the old artwork. Home, Discover, Search, the detail and stream screens and the add-on manager now all carry the new ripple mark. v0.16.0: - Changed: Rivulet has a new logo - concentric ripple rings around a play button, the "drop hits water" reading of the name. It replaces the old mark everywhere: the addon icon, the repository icon, both fanart backdrops and the project site. Flat by design, one teal-to-indigo accent, no glow - the old mark had both and neither survived small sizes. - Improved: a round of measured performance work, aimed squarely at Raspberry Pi and TV boxes. Playback starts sooner when several subtitle add-ons are installed - they are now asked together instead of one after another, so one slow add-on no longer delays every play by its full timeout. The stream list no longer redraws itself completely every time a late add-on answers; new sources are appended under your cursor instead. Opening the addon from a favourite, a widget or a Settings button loads noticeably less code, as does the background service at every Kodi boot. - Improved: less strain on SD cards and eMMC. The metadata cache no longer rewrites its whole file once per fetched title - a cold "Continue watching" open now writes once instead of up to fifteen times - and reopening the row when everything is already cached writes nothing at all. The playback-progress bookkeeping that runs every 15 seconds during playback does a fraction of the work it did. And the streaming server's log file, which only ever rotated at startup, is now kept bounded for the whole session, however many days Kodi stays up. - Fix: on Android TV boxes, where the embedded streaming server can never run, the background service kept re-checking for it every 5 seconds for the entire session - over 17,000 pointless wake-ups a day. It now checks once every 5 minutes, and still notices an external server appearing at your Server URL within that window. v0.15.0: - New: a "Continue watching" row at the top of Home. Rivulet has recorded where you stopped in every title since 0.5.0 - it is what drives the resume prompt - but there was no way to see what you were in the middle of, so getting back into a half-watched series meant remembering what it was and going looking for it. The new row lists the titles you are partway through, most recent first, one entry per series however many episodes you have started. It appears only when there is actually something to resume, and can be switched off in Settings - Home screen. Picking a title works exactly like picking it anywhere else, resume prompt included. To make room for a ninth row, Home's menu rows are slightly more compact. - Improved: the grey plate behind Home's account status line is gone. It was the one place a hairline colour was used as a 720x48 fill, and it read as a grey slab - most obviously when logged out, where the short "Not logged in" left most of it empty. The coloured status dot and the dark backdrop already carry the information, so nothing is lost. v0.14.0: - New: Rivulet can open itself when Kodi starts. On a box that exists to run Rivulet, every boot ended with the same walk into Videos to launch the addon; the new "Open Rivulet automatically on Kodi startup" switch in Settings - Home screen does that walk for you. Off by default, and it waits for the skin to finish coming up before launching, so it cannot open into a half-drawn screen. - Fix: scrolling through a catalog that was still loading in the background threw the selection back to the first poster every time a page arrived, and the further you had scrolled the more violent the jump. The cursor now stays on the poster you were looking at while the rest of the list fills in behind it. v0.13.0: - Fix: opening a catalog showed only the first page the add-on chose to serve and gave you no way to reach the rest. Some lists serve 20 titles at a time, so a 400-title list opened as 20. Catalogs are now walked in full: the poster browser opens straight away on the first page and the rest fill in behind you as they arrive, rather than making you wait for the whole list. A catalog that does not page still costs a single request, exactly as before. v0.12.0: - Fix: catalogs that are not film, series or anime had become unreachable. 0.10.0 replaced the single "Discover" row with one row per type, and anything an add-on published outside those three - a whole add-on's worth of catalogs, or the "anime.movie" and "anime.series" that some publish - had nowhere left to appear. On one setup that hid 20 of 51 installed catalogs, including every catalog of one add-on. Home now has an "Other" row for whatever Movies, Series and Anime do not cover. It appears only if you have such an add-on installed, and can be switched off in Settings like the other three. The three rows also recognise a type's base now, so "anime.movie" and "anime.series" list under Anime. v0.11.0: - Fix: the poster browser printed every title twice - once as the large heading, and again in small type over the artwork of the focused poster, where it landed on top of whatever that poster already had in its lower-left corner. The copy over the artwork is gone; the heading stays. - Fix: opening Settings dropped you straight into the Server URL box in edit mode, where the arrow keys typed into the box instead of moving between settings, so Back was the only way out. Server URL now sits in "Streaming server" underneath the "Run embedded server" switch, and Settings opens on that switch instead. Your existing address is kept. v0.10.0: - New: Home opens straight into Movies, Series or Anime. Each row lists only the catalogs of that type, headed by the add-on publishing them, so the type is no longer repeated on every line and two add-ons offering "Popular" are finally told apart. - New: Rivulet's own progress, countdown, busy, confirmation and picker dialogs. Kodi drew these in whatever skin you use, so mid-flow the add-on dropped out of its own look entirely; they now match the rest of the screens. - New: the "next episode in N seconds" countdown can be skipped with OK to play immediately. Previously OK did nothing and the only key that worked was BACK, which cancelled it. - Improved: buffering no longer redraws the whole "Preparing stream" panel for every chunk received; only the numbers that actually changed are written. v0.9.1: - Fix: the background artwork was far darker than intended on Home, the poster browser and the stream list. 0.9.0 redrew the screens but left the previous interface's dimming underneath the new one, so the two stacked: on Home the fanart came out roughly twice as dark as it was meant to, and on the right of the screen it was almost invisible. Every screen's backdrop now uses the brightness the design actually calls for. - Fix: the poster browser had a faint horizontal band running across it, about three quarters of the way down, where two parts of the background shading met. It is gone, and the shading behind the posters is now one continuous fade. - Fix: four labels stayed in English whatever language Kodi was set to - the heading above the source list, and the Add-ons, Discover and Search screen names in each of those screens' headers. All four now follow Kodi's language setting. No new translations were needed; the words were already translated and simply were not being used. - Improved: in the stream list, a source's resolution badge is now outlined rather than filled unless that row is selected, so the highlighted source stands out instead of every row competing for attention. A source with no cache information now shows a dash instead of leaving a gap in the column. - Improved: the account line on the Home screen has a small status dot - accent-coloured when you are logged in, dim when you are not. - Improved: a series' episode list is slightly wider, giving long episode titles more room before they are cut off. v0.9.0: - Changed: every Rivulet screen has been redrawn for a television. The windows are now authored at 1920x1080 instead of 1280x720, so text is roughly half again as large and readable from a sofa rather than a desk. Selection now looks the same everywhere - the highlighted row is filled and marked with a bright blue bar down its left edge - where before each screen did its own thing. Nothing moved: the same screens are in the same places and every key does what it did. - New: the stream list no longer crams everything into one long line. A source's resolution is now a colour-coded badge, and its size, seeder count and whether it is cached each have their own column, so you can compare sources down the screen instead of reading each row end to end. The release type and the codec/HDR tags are separated too, and the panel on the left counts how many sources, how many add-ons and how many cached results the search actually returned. - New: a series' screen now tells you what you are looking at - how many seasons it has, how many episodes are in the season you are on, and its year and rating. Episode numbers are separated from episode titles rather than run together. - New: episodes you started but did not finish now show how far you got, as a bar under the thumbnail and a percentage beside it. Rivulet already recorded this locally for the resume prompt; it was simply never shown. - New: the poster browser now names where you are - the add-on and catalog you opened, or the search you ran - instead of an anonymous header. - Fix: the "%d%% WATCHED", source-count and season/episode-count labels, and the on-screen key hints, are translated in all fourteen languages Rivulet ships rather than being English-only. - Note: Kodi does not let an add-on ship its own fonts - a window can only use fonts the skin you are running defines. Rivulet's screens ask for the sizes Estuary provides, which is Kodi's default skin. On a third-party skin that does not define them, Kodi substitutes its own default font and the type scale will look flatter than intended; everything remains legible and usable. v0.8.0: - Changed: Rivulet now has one interface instead of two. It had quietly carried both its own screens and an older set of plain Kodi folder listings, and keeping both was not free for you: the browse-by-year and cast-and-crew features in 0.7.0 went into the old listings only, which is why they seemed missing until 0.7.1 added them a second time. The old listings are gone, so everything now lives in one place and a new feature can only arrive in the screens you actually use. Nothing you navigate to day to day changes. - Improved: searching for an actor, director or writer now puts their real credits first on every screen. That ranking previously existed only in the old listings, so the search you actually used did not have it. - Improved: a title's actors are now handed to Kodi while it plays, so the cast shows up in Kodi's own playback info alongside the title and artwork. - Note: if you saved a Kodi favourite pointing at one of Rivulet's old folder listings, or used one in a skin widget, it will no longer open that listing - it now lands on a short screen offering Settings. Open Rivulet normally instead. Playing a saved stream link still works. v0.7.1: - Fix: catalog rows named "Search" did nothing whatsoever when picked. Some add-ons - The Movie Database add-on among them - publish catalogs that can only be searched, never browsed, and Rivulet listed them anyway and then silently gave up. Picking one now asks what you are looking for and searches that catalog, and those rows are marked "search only" so they read differently before you pick them. A catalog that comes back empty, or an add-on that fails, now says so instead of appearing to ignore you. - Fix: browsing by year was effectively unreachable, and so was a title's cast and crew. Both arrived in 0.7.0 but only on Rivulet's plain directory listings, not on the screens you actually navigate. Cinemeta's "New" catalog now opens straight into its list of years - 2026 back to 1920 - because that catalog cannot be browsed without one; and every other catalog that offers genres exposes them on the context menu (the "C" key, or your remote's menu button), leaving normal browsing exactly as it was. Cast and crew is on the same context-menu button while you are looking at a title, on the poster coverflow and on a series' episode screen. Pick an actor, director or writer to see what else they worked on. - Fix: two Cinemeta catalogs, "Last videos" and "Calendar videos", were listed but could never show anything - they need information only Stremio's own home screen supplies. They are no longer offered. v0.7.0: - New: browse a catalog by year, or by genre. Stremio add-ons can declare which filters each of their catalogs supports, and Cinemeta declares over a hundred years as well as every genre - so the "New" catalog now opens with a Filter row listing 2026 back to 1920, and "Popular" and "Featured" list genres. Pick one and the catalog reloads filtered; the row then reads "Filter: 1972" so you can see what is applied, and offers Clear filter to drop it again. Catalogs that declare no filters are unchanged. - New: find a title's cast and crew, and everything else they worked on. Every film and series row now has a "Cast & crew" entry in its context menu, listing the actors, directors and writers the add-on reported. Pick a name and Rivulet searches for that person across every add-on you have installed; pick a genre and it opens that catalog. Results that genuinely credit the person are listed first, ahead of titles that merely mention the name - nothing is hidden, because a Stremio search matches titles and credits alike and there is no way to ask an add-on for one without the other. - New: Rivulet now hands a title's actors to Kodi itself, so the cast appears in Kodi's own info dialog and anywhere else your skin shows it. - Fix: several parts of the interface were shown in English whatever language Kodi was set to. Twelve of the thirteen translations were missing all five of the Home screen's row descriptions, and the two progress messages you see on every search and every stream lookup had never been translatable at all, along with the season bar, the "Not logged in" status and two add-on management messages. All of them are now translated in every language Rivulet ships. The check that was supposed to catch this only verified that translations contained nothing unknown to English, never that they covered it, so it is now pinned both ways - including that no translation loses a "%s", which would have failed mid-dialog. - Fix: installing Rivulet's recommended advancedsettings.xml is now atomic. Interrupted halfway - a power cut, routine on a TV box or Raspberry Pi running off an SD card - it could leave a half-written file, which Kodi then discards entirely; and because Rivulet never overwrites an existing advancedsettings.xml, that broken file could never be repaired by installing it again. v0.6.1: - Fix: stopping a stalled stream still took the best part of a minute before Kodi responded. 0.5.6 blamed the wrong network timeout; the one that actually governs it is the low-speed window Kodi applies to playback reads, which a stalled stream sits in at zero bytes per second until it expires. It is now Kodi's own default instead of triple it, taking a stop from around 57 seconds to around 20. Not instant - an add-on cannot interrupt Kodi's own reader - but a third of the wait. NOTE: if you already installed Rivulet's advancedsettings.xml it is never overwritten, so edit curllowspeedtime to 20 yourself, or delete the file and re-install it from Settings. v0.6.0: - New: add-ons are now queried all at once instead of one after another, and the stream list opens as soon as the first one answers rather than waiting for the slowest. If you run several stream add-ons this removes whichever is slowest or unreachable from the wait; if you run only one, there is nothing to overlap and you will not notice a difference. Remaining results drop in live while you are already browsing, with a line telling you more are still on the way, and the row you have highlighted stays highlighted as the list re-orders around it. - Fix: an add-on still waiting on its timeout could keep Rivulet running in the background after you had already left the stream list, which could hold up Kodi. Those lookups are now abandoned the moment you walk away. v0.5.8: - Fix: with "play next episode automatically" enabled, stopping an episode yourself started the next one anyway. Stopping is you saying you are done, so it now returns to the stream list and stays there; the next episode only auto-plays when an episode actually finishes. The same applied to stopping an episode that had been auto-played - that no longer keeps the chain going either. - New: Rivulet now tells you when it has been updated. Kodi installs add-on updates silently, so the first time you open Rivulet after a new version lands you get a brief notification saying which version you are now on. It appears once per update, never on a fresh install. v0.5.7: - Fix: Rivulet would start playing a torrent as soon as the first half-megabyte arrived, even when the swarm was far too slow to keep up - so playback began and then stalled seconds later. It now checks the measured download speed first: if the source cannot fill the rest of your configured buffer almost immediately, it keeps buffering (showing live speed and peer count, cancellable) instead of starting into a stall. Fast sources still start just as quickly as before, and a slow-but-working source still plays rather than buffering forever. v0.5.6: - Fix: pressing stop on a stalled torrent could leave Kodi frozen for up to three minutes. Rivulet's recommended advancedsettings.xml doubled Kodi's network timeout, and Kodi waits for the reader to give up before it can finish stopping. That timeout is back to Kodi's own value, with one retry instead of two, so stopping a stuck stream is now bounded at about a minute in the worst case. Patience with slow-but-moving torrents is unaffected - that is a separate setting, left as it was. NOTE: if you already installed Rivulet's advancedsettings.xml, it is never overwritten - edit it yourself, or delete it and re-install it from Settings, to pick this up. - Fix: the log claimed "pre-buffer complete" when playback had in fact started early on a partly-filled buffer, which was misleading in exactly the logs where it mattered - a stream stalling seconds after it started. It now says which of the two happened. v0.5.5: - Fix: Rivulet's icon, fanart and screenshot gallery were missing in Kodi's own Add-ons browser when installing from the Rivulet repository. The repository was publishing those images to different paths than the ones the add-on declares, so Kodi asked for them and got nothing back. The screenshots added in 0.4.20 should finally be visible. - Improved: the metadata cache now keeps itself under a fixed size budget rather than a fixed number of titles. A TV series entry is far bigger than a film's (it lists every episode), so the old limit could let the cache grow to a few megabytes and rewrite all of it each time a title was cached - the opposite of what it was there for on SD-card and eMMC installs. v0.5.4: - Fix: seeder counts were missing from nearly every Torrentio result, and the few that did appear were usually wrong. Torrentio states the count before the file size, which Rivulet was not reading, so it fell back to guessing at other numbers in the release name. It now reads Torrentio's own marker: the count is correct on every row, and sorting by seeders works properly. Checked against 100 live Torrentio results. v0.5.3: - Improved: a long stream list now uses about half the memory it did, and writes about half as much to storage. Each row carries a hidden copy of its stream details, which is now compressed - roughly 200KB less on a title that returns several hundred sources. Best felt on TV boxes and SD-card installs, where storage writes are the scarce resource. - Improved: Kodi 19 loads one less module on every navigation. v0.5.2: - Improved: every screen opens faster. Rivulet used to load its whole network stack on each navigation, even on screens that never go online - the Home screen now loads a fifth of the code it did before, and the stream list, player and catalog views open around four times sooner. Most noticeable on TV boxes, Raspberry Pi and other low-power devices. - Improved: long stream lists appear sooner - the text tidy-up that runs over every row is about eight times quicker, which adds up over the hundreds of sources a popular title returns. - Improved: stepping through a show's seasons no longer re-downloads that title's details once per season; they are reused for a few minutes. - Improved: the poster coverflow scrolls more smoothly - the background image is no longer re-sent to the skin on keypresses that do not change the highlighted title. - Improved: Rivulet re-reads its add-on list and saved state from disk far less often, writes its playback progress more compactly, and the background service no longer touches the disk every couple of seconds while nothing is playing - less wear on SD cards and internal storage. v0.5.1: - New: the stream list's second line now describes the file itself - audio format and channel layout, languages, bitrate, release group and tracker - instead of repeating the add-on name. - New: debrid sources say whether they are ready to play: the service code shows green when the file is cached and orange with "DL" when it still has to be downloaded first. Torrentio, Comet, StremThru and every built-in AIOStreams format are recognised. - New: Dolby Vision profile markers (P5/P7/P8, FEL, MEL, BL+RPU, Hybrid) and editions like IMAX, Extended or REPACK now show on the row, so a native DV remux can be told apart from a re-mapped conversion without starting playback first. - Improved: the add-on name moved to the end of the first line, and is dropped entirely when every source came from the same add-on. v0.5.0: - New: the next episode now plays automatically when one finishes, with a cancellable countdown, preferring a release from the same group as the episode you just watched. Turn it off, or change the countdown, under Playback. - New: what you watch is now written back to your Stremio account - progress, resume position and watched state - and Rivulet offers to resume where you left off. Progress is kept locally too, so resume works logged out. - New: RAR/ZIP/7z/TAR/TGZ, NZB and FTP streams now play through the streaming server instead of silently failing. - Fix: magnet links whose info hash is in Base32 form no longer produce an unplayable link, and percent-encoded trackers are decoded before use. - Fix: the player's info panel no longer reads "Not available" - it now shows the title's own description, falling back to the release/size/seeders of the file playing. - Improved: streams that can only be opened in the Stremio app now say so instead of failing as "no playable stream". - Improved: seeder counts in the stream list are marked with a triangle instead of the old "S50" prefix, and subtitle add-ons' own labels are carried through. v0.4.22: - Fix: while a stream was playing, play/pause and the on-screen playback controls did nothing until you backed out of the addon and returned to the video - every Rivulet screen is a Kodi modal dialog, and Kodi sends all input to the topmost dialog rather than to the player. All open screens now step aside when playback starts and come back exactly where you left them when it ends. - Fix: the player's info panel showed "Not available" with a placeholder image instead of the title and poster of what you picked. - Improved: torrent streams now report their real file name to Kodi, so the correct media type is used instead of leaving Kodi to guess. v0.4.21: - Fix: 32-bit Android and Android TV devices (e.g. Chromecast with Google TV) were detected as an unknown CPU architecture (armv8l) and the server-binary download failed with "No release asset for this platform". - Fix: on Android the addon now says up front that the embedded streaming server cannot run there and to point Server URL at a server running elsewhere, instead of failing with a confusing download error. - Improved: a downloaded server binary is now verified to be executable, and the "no release asset" message now names the detected platform. v0.4.20: - New: README and the project site now show a real screenshot gallery of the current UI, generated by a new scripts/capture_screenshots.py (drives a running Kodi over its JSON-RPC socket). - New: Kodi's own Add-ons browser now shows real screenshots for Rivulet instead of empty placeholders. v0.4.19: - Fix: quitting Kodi while the streaming-server binary was still auto-downloading no longer hangs shutdown until the download finishes. - Fix: a crashed embedded server now releases its log file immediately on restart. - Improved: stream resolution and Stremio account requests now reuse HTTP connections - snappier browsing and playback start on slow devices. v0.4.18: - Fix: Home screen's second line per row (e.g. "Browse catalogs from your installed addons" under Discover) was a hardcoded English literal that never translated, even when the row's own main label correctly did (e.g. "Scopri" in Italian). Now localized like every other string. v0.4.17: - New: Rivulet's UI is now translated - Italian, German, French, Spanish, Portuguese (Brazil), Dutch, Russian, Polish, Turkish, Chinese (Simplified), Japanese, Korean and Arabic, on top of English. The language follows Kodi's own interface-language setting automatically (Settings > Interface > Language), with no addon setting to configure. v0.4.16: - New: the embedded stremio-server's full configuration is now exposed under Settings (5 new sections: BitTorrent, Server resources, Server proxy, Server add-ons, Server diagnostics) - peer/tracker/encryption tuning, memory caps, idle-torrent timeout, proxy relay, Bitmagnet/Torznab indexers, DLNA casting and more, instead of only being controllable via environment variables. Changing any of them restarts the embedded server automatically, same as the existing Server URL setting already does. v0.4.15: - Fix: pressing Back from search results fell straight through to the Home menu instead of returning to the previous screen (Search had no screen of its own to return to). - New: Search now remembers past queries (clearable) and lets you re-run one instead of retyping - Kodi's on-screen keyboard has no live-typing autocomplete, so this history list is the closest equivalent. v0.4.14: - Fix: Settings > Account had no way to log in - clicking "Sync addons now" while logged out just said "Login to Stremio" with nowhere to do it. Added dedicated Login/Logout buttons there. - Fix: the Kodi repository add-on used a schema Kodi 21+ no longer supports ("no directory matching" error) and could not be installed/updated on Kodi 21. v0.4.13: - New: a Kodi add-on repository (repository.rivulet) is now published, so Rivulet can update itself automatically instead of needing a manual zip reinstall for every release. - New: a project site with install instructions and docs is published to GitHub Pages. v0.4.12: - New: Library and Add-ons now have their own custom screens (no more dropping to the classical Kodi directory). - New: Add-ons screen lets you install from a manifest URL and remove addons directly. - New: the streams screen shows year, runtime, rating and genres, and drops repeated provider names when every source is from the same addon. - New: Discover's poster wall fades softly at both edges instead of a hard cut. - Fix: backing out of a nested screen (Discover, a title's sources, ...) now correctly returns to the previous screen instead of sometimes jumping back to the Home menu. v0.4.11: - Fix: playback now takes the screen immediately - video no longer starts hidden behind the menu until you press Back. - Fix: stopping playback no longer briefly spawns a duplicate Home screen. v0.4.10: - Fix: an addon that's briefly unavailable no longer freezes the UI - streams/search now query addons in parallel instead of one at a time. - Fix: an expired Stremio session now prompts a clean re-login instead of silently failing. - Fix: installed addons' info now refreshes automatically instead of going stale forever. - Fix: a rare crash could leave a screen stuck open; screens now always close properly. - Fix: two addon actions running at the same time could silently lose one of them - now safely retried. - Security: the streaming server binary download now always verifies its integrity before installing. v0.4.9: - Fix: logging in no longer wipes addons you installed while logged out - addon sync is now a proper two-way sync. - New: Settings > Account > "Sync addons now" to force and confirm a sync. - New: a loading spinner (with progress and cancel) now shows during Search/Discover/Streams lookups instead of a frozen screen. - Fix: the app icon's logo graphic is now properly centered. v0.4.8: - Fix: movies no longer show a pointless "Play" step - pick a movie and go straight to sources. - Fix: a stray "[/B]" no longer shows on the top stream row. - Fix: Library and Add-ons no longer fail to open from the new Home. - Home menu got icons, short descriptions and a login-status line. v0.4.7: - New: a custom, non-standard Home/Discover/Search/Detail/Streams UI (Library/Add-ons/Settings still classic). - Showcase now reports errors (notification + log) instead of failing silently.

extension.description: Add this repository to Kodi to install Rivulet and receive automatic updates.
extension.news: v1.0.2: - Changed: the new Rivulet ripple logo. The artwork shipped with 0.16.0's rebrand, but a repository addon only refetches its icon when its own version changes - this release exists to carry that change to installed copies.
